Air handling unit controller · BACnet points list

CAREL k.air air handling unit controller BACnet points list

Updated 12 November 2026

Short answer

k.air is CAREL's ready-made air handling unit controller. Its manual has a supervisor variable table with a Modbus address and a BACnet object for every variable: about 4,350 objects covering BMS commands, setpoints, every sensor and output (with its configuration), fan, humidifier, compressor and heat recovery data, and one alarm BV per alarm. Most of the list is configuration; an integrator normally maps a small part of it.

This page lists 4350 BACnet objects for the CAREL k.air air handling unit controller — 2473 of them writable — with each object’s type, instance number, name, engineering units and access. It is re-typed from CAREL’s own free documentation, linked below.

BMS integration notes: CAREL k.air air handling unit controller

Integration in brief

Enable BMS on/off with BV 234, then switch the unit with BV 2 and select summer or winter with BV 4. Write the comfort temperature setpoints (AV 2585 winter, AV 2584 summer) if the BMS owns them. Read the unit status (PIV 3645), the supply, return and room temperatures, and the generic alarm BV 902; BV 1 resets alarms. Configure the BMS offline alarm (PIV 2898/2899) if the BMS should be supervised.

Minimum points to map

The short list most integrators start with — enough to run the unit from a BMS. Map more as the job needs.

ObjectNameWhyAccess
BV 234Scheduler_OnOffUnit.BMS_OnOff_EnMust be on for the BMS on/off command to workWrite
BV 2Scheduler_OnOffUnit.BMS_OnOffUnit on/off command from the BMSWrite
BV 4SummerWinter_BMSSummer/winter command (0 = summer, 1 = winter)Write
AV 2585UnitSetP.TempSetP.Winter.ComfortWinter comfort temperature setpointWrite
AV 2584UnitSetP.TempSetP.Summer.ComfortSummer comfort temperature setpointWrite
BV 1AlarmsMng.AlrmResByBmsAlarm resetWrite
PIV 3645SchedStatusActive status: 0 off, 1 economy, 2 pre-comfort, 3 comfortRead
AV 3435SupplyTemp.Val_Hw_RSupply air temperature (probe reading)Read
AV 3442RetTemp.Val_RReturn air temperatureRead
BV 902GlobalAlrm_Dout.Val_WGeneric alarm activeRead

Enable & remote start

The unit can be switched by keypad/th-Tune, BMS, digital input and scheduler; any enabled source set to off stops it. BMS on/off works only when BV 234 (enable on/off request by BMS) is on; BV 2 then turns the unit on or off.

Heartbeat & communication loss

PIV 2898 selects BMS offline handling (0 disabled, 1 warning only, 2 alarm, 3 alarm with timeout) and PIV 2899 sets the timeout, 120 s by default. BV 1347 shows the BMS offline alarm.

Network setup

  • Choose the BACnet port in menu Y: BMS Line or BMS2 Line = 2 (BACnet MS/TP on RS485) or Ethernet 2 Line = 1 (BACnet IP).
  • Y003 sets the BACnet device instance (also the MS/TP station address); baud rate, parity and stop bits are in menu Y too.

Watch out for

  • Most of the ~4,350 objects are I/O configuration (board, channel, probe type, limits); writing them changes the unit's set-up.
  • Setpoints exist per season and per mode (economy, pre-comfort, comfort); the current setpoint values are read-only status objects.
  • Object instances are not derived from the Modbus address; use the table, not a formula.

Integration notes

  • The table gives Modbus classes, not a BACnet access column. Access here follows the Modbus class: coils and holding registers W, discrete inputs and input registers R.
  • Object names are the CAREL variable names from the table. No engineering units are printed; descriptions carry the Modbus address, value meanings, and a 32-bit flag for Dim 2 variables.
  • Repeated rows in the source were dropped (CS112, DI1159, HR614/615, IR118/119, IR626-632). On page 136 the source repeats 12 rows from page 133 (DI340-DI366) between wrapped variable names; those repeats were dropped and the wrapped names joined.
  • One printed instance clash is kept as printed: BV 1436 (DI1210) for two ZA return fan alarms. The CoilRegOffset row on page 144 is garbled (it repeats HR143/PIV1666 and PIV1667 from the previous page next to HR192/AV1715); it is listed as AV 1715 (Modbus HR192), which fits the table's sequence. OA_CoilActMode is printed as PI4577 and listed as PIV 4577.
  • The supervisor table skips some Modbus addresses; a few objects (for example AV 3436) appear only in the manual's parameter tables and are not in this list.
  • Which serial or Ethernet port speaks BACnet is set in menu Y (BMS Line or BMS2 Line = BACnet MS/TP, Ethernet 2 Line = BACnet IP).

Check it against the live device. A points list tells you what the controller can expose; the unit in front of you may differ by firmware or installed options. This list is provided as-is for reference only and may contain mistakes — confirming it before you write, map or commission anything is up to you (terms). Questions about the CAREL k.air air handling unit controller

How many BACnet points does the CAREL k.air air handling unit controller have?

This list has 4350 BACnet objects: 739 analog values, 1596 binary values, 136 integer values, 1879 positive integer values. The exact set on a given unit depends on its firmware, installed options and configuration.

Which CAREL k.air air handling unit controller BACnet points are writable?

2473 of the 4350 objects accept a write. Points marked Command have a priority array: a write holds until it is released, so release it back to automatic when you are done. The source has no read/write column, so this is inferred from object type.

Where is the official CAREL k.air air handling unit controller BACnet documentation?

The source is k.air - Air handling unit controller, user manual (11. Supervisor variable table) (+030220981), revision rel. 1.8 - 2026-06-25, published free by CAREL at https://www.carel.com/documents/10191/0/%2B030220981/14d83d46-c7fc-403d-b38d-2688a78559ef?version=1.11.

What are the minimum BACnet points to integrate the CAREL k.air air handling unit controller?

Start with BV 234 Scheduler_OnOffUnit.BMS_OnOff_En (Must be on for the BMS on/off command to work); BV 2 Scheduler_OnOffUnit.BMS_OnOff (Unit on/off command from the BMS); BV 4 SummerWinter_BMS (Summer/winter command (0 = summer, 1 = winter)); AV 2585 UnitSetP.TempSetP.Winter.Comfort (Winter comfort temperature setpoint); AV 2584 UnitSetP.TempSetP.Summer.Comfort (Summer comfort temperature setpoint); BV 1 AlarmsMng.AlrmResByBms (Alarm reset); PIV 3645 SchedStatus (Active status: 0 off, 1 economy, 2 pre-comfort, 3 comfort); AV 3435 SupplyTemp.Val_Hw_R (Supply air temperature (probe reading)); AV 3442 RetTemp.Val_R (Return air temperature); BV 902 GlobalAlrm_Dout.Val_W (Generic alarm active).

How do I enable BMS control of the CAREL k.air air handling unit controller?

The unit can be switched by keypad/th-Tune, BMS, digital input and scheduler; any enabled source set to off stops it. BMS on/off works only when BV 234 (enable on/off request by BMS) is on; BV 2 then turns the unit on or off.

Does the CAREL k.air air handling unit controller need a BACnet heartbeat or have a communication timeout?

PIV 2898 selects BMS offline handling (0 disabled, 1 warning only, 2 alarm, 3 alarm with timeout) and PIV 2899 sets the timeout, 120 s by default. BV 1347 shows the BMS offline alarm.

How do I check these points on the real k.air air handling unit controller?

Scan the network with a BACnet IP browser such as Easy BACnet, open the device and compare its object list with this table. Anything missing is usually an option that isn't installed or a point that is disabled in the controller's configuration.
